questions.question: In 1848, who prepared a series of four prints visualising a world made up of 'democratic and social Republics'?
questions.explanation: In 1848, Frédéric Sorrieu, a French artist, prepared a famous series of four prints visualising his utopian dream of a world made up of democratic and social Republics.

questions.question: What was the official name of the Civil Code of 1804 introduced in France?
questions.explanation: The Civil Code of 1804 was officially known as the Napoleonic Code. It established equality before the law and abolished birth privileges.

questions.question: A customs union named 'Zollverein' formed in 1834 at the initiative of Prussia was primarily aimed at:
options: Abolishing tariff barriers and reducing currencies from over thirty to two
Establishing a military alliance against Britain
Promoting absolute monarchy across the German states
questions.explanation: Zollverein abolished tariff barriers and reduced the number of currencies in the German states from over thirty to two, creating an integrated economic territory.

questions.question: Who hosted the Congress of Vienna in 1815 following the defeat of Napoleon?
questions.explanation: The Congress of Vienna in 1815 was hosted by Austrian Chancellor Duke Metternich to restore conservative order across post-Napoleonic Europe.

questions.question: Giuseppe Mazzini founded two underground societies named:
options: Young Italy in Marseilles and Young Europe in Berne
Carbonari in Rome and Red Shirts in Sicily
Jacobin Club in Paris and Bolsheviks in Moscow
Liberals of Frankfurt and Zollverein of Prussia
questions.explanation: Giuseppe Mazzini founded 'Young Italy' in Marseilles and 'Young Europe' in Berne to promote republican national unification.

questions.question: Duke Metternich described Giuseppe Mazzini as:
options: 'The most dangerous enemy of our social order'
questions.explanation: Due to Mazzini's relentless opposition to monarchy and his vision of democratic republics, Metternich called him 'the most dangerous enemy of our social order'.

questions.question: Which treaty recognized Greece as an independent nation in 1832?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 recognized Greece as an independent nation, ending Ottoman control after the Greek War of Independence.

questions.question: Which famous English poet organized funds and fought in the Greek War of Independence, dying of fever in 1824?
questions.explanation: English poet Lord Byron organized funds and later went to fight in Greece, where he died of fever in 1824.

questions.question: Where did the 831 elected representatives assemble to convene the Frankfurt Parliament on 18 May 1848?
options: Church of St. Paul in Frankfurt
questions.explanation: On 18 May 1848, 831 elected representatives marched in a festive procession to take their places in the Frankfurt Parliament convened in the Church of St. Paul.

questions.question: In January 1871, who was proclaimed the German Emperor in an unheated Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles?
questions.explanation: In January 1871, Prussian King William I was proclaimed German Emperor at the Palace of Versailles following the victory in the Franco-Prussian War.

questions.question: Who was the chief architect of German unification that carried out the process with the help of the Prussian army and bureaucracy?
questions.explanation: Prussia's Chief Minister Otto von Bismarck was the chief architect of German unification, utilizing diplomacy and three victorious wars over seven years.

questions.question: During the middle of the 19th century, which was the only Italian state ruled by an Italian princely house?
questions.explanation: Italy was divided into seven states, of which only Sardinia-Piedmont was ruled by an Italian princely house under King Victor Emmanuel II.

questions.question: Who was the Chief Minister of Sardinia-Piedmont who engineered the diplomatic alliance with France to defeat Austrian forces in 1859?
questions.explanation: Count Camillo de Cavour, Chief Minister of Sardinia-Piedmont, neither a revolutionary nor a democrat, engineered a tactful diplomatic alliance with France to defeat Austrian forces in 1859.

questions.question: Which famous leader led the 'Expedition of the Thousand' to South Italy and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1860 with his volunteer Red Shirts?
questions.explanation: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the armed volunteers (popularly known as Red Shirts) in the Expedition of the Thousand into Southern Italy and drove out the Spanish rulers.

questions.question: The Act of Union (1707) between England and which country resulted in the formation of the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain'?
questions.explanation: The Act of Union (1707) between England and Scotland created the United Kingdom of Great Britain, enabling England to impose influence over Scotland.

questions.question: After a failed revolt led by Wolfe Tone and his United Irishmen (1798), Ireland was forcibly incorporated into the United Kingdom in:
questions.explanation: Following the suppression of Wolfe Tone's revolt of 1798, Ireland was forcibly incorporated into the United Kingdom in 1801 under the Act of Union.

questions.question: What was the female allegory of France christened, representing the idea of a people's nation?
questions.explanation: In France, the nation was allegorized as Marianne, a popular Christian name, characterized by the red cap, the tricolour, and the cockade.

questions.question: The visual allegory of Germany, Germania, wears a crown of oak leaves because the German oak stands for:
questions.explanation: Visual attributes assigned to Germania include a crown of oak leaves, as the German oak historically symbolizes heroism.

questions.question: The vast geographical and ethnic region of the Balkans under Ottoman control was inhabited broadly by people known as:
questions.explanation: The inhabitants of the Balkan region comprising modern-day Romania, Bulgaria, Albania, Greece, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbia, etc., were broadly known as Slavs.

questions.subtopic: Balkan Conflict and World War I
questions.question: Why did the Balkan region become the primary source of intense nationalist tension in Europe after 1871?
options: Due to explosive spread of romantic nationalism alongside the disintegration of the Ottoman Empire and big power rivalry
Because Napoleon conquered and annexed all the Balkan states
Because of religious conflicts between Protestant and Catholic churches
Because of the discovery of gold mines across Macedonia
questions.explanation: The spread of romantic nationalism coupled with the decay of the Ottoman Empire and rivalry among European superpowers (Russia, Germany, England, Austro-Hungary) turned the Balkans into a powder keg leading directly to World War I.
